assumptions: RDKit's descriptors and medchem's rule and alert definitions.
limits: Rules flag; they do not predict activity.
bio.jane/contract.question: What are this molecule's RDKit descriptors, drug-likeness rule results and structural alerts?

description: Assess a small molecule given as SMILES or a molfile: RDKit's descriptors, medchem's drug-likeness rules (Lipinski, Veber, Ghose, Egan, REOS, rule of three, CNS and more) and the papers' own readings where medchem departs from them, with every bound and this molecule's value, a structural-alert screen (PAINS, Brenk, NIH, ZINC and ChEMBL's seven curated sets) with the matched atoms, the molecular formula with its masses and natural-abundance isotope pattern, QED drug-likeness under all three weightings, ESOL aqueous solubility, synthetic accessibility and natural-product likeness, the Bemis–Murcko scaffold and generic framework, the BOILED-Egg's gut-absorption and brain-penetration verdicts, and per-atom logP, polar-surface and charge contributions. Readings are taken with hydrogens implicit, the form the descriptors and the rules' papers assume. An alert flags a nuisance or reactive substructure; it is not a verdict on activity or toxicity.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alert_sets.description: which structural-alert catalogs to screen against. Empty screens nothing, which is not a clean result.

molecule.description: the structure: a SMILES string or an MDL molfile (V2000 or V3000). One molecule; for an SDF, pass one record.

rules.description: which drug-likeness rules to evaluate, by id: medchem's 17, plus the papers' own readings of Lipinski, Ghose and REOS (ids ending _paper). Every rule by default.

name: assess_small_molecule

alerts.description: every alert matched: its set, name, SMARTS and the atom indices of the first match, numbered on the implicit-hydrogen molecule

atom_contributions.description: per-atom weights on the implicit-hydrogen molecule: logp (Crippen, heavy atoms), tpsa (Ertl, N and O), tpsaSP (Ertl with S and P) and charge (Gasteiger–Marsili; not a number around an element RDKit has no parameters for)

bioavailability_radar.description: SwissADME's Bioavailability Radar (Daina 2017): six axes (lipo, size, polar, insolu, insatu, flex) with this molecule's value, the inclusive window, whether it is inside, and drugLike when all six are; read with Crippen logP for XLOGP3 and the XLOGP3 window's figure bound of 5.0

boiled_egg.description: the BOILED-Egg placement (Daina & Zoete 2016) of the neutral, unsalted ChEMBL parent as the paper places it (`placed` says whether that is the parent or, when the pipeline refuses one or it is the molecule itself, the record as drawn; `asDrawn` and `parent` carry both): tPSA counting S and P, RDKit's Crippen logP standing in for WLOGP, and for the gut-absorption (hia) and brain-penetration (bbb) ellipses whether the point is inside, its summed focal distance and the ellipse's major axis; region is yolk, white or outside

canonical_smiles.description: RDKit's canonical SMILES of the molecule every reading was taken on

descriptors.description: RDKit's descriptors under RDKit's own keys (exactmw, CrippenClogP, tpsa, NumHBD …)

formula.description: RDKit's molecular formula (every hydrogen, isotope labels merged, charge suffixed) with its element counts and charge, the monoisotopic and average masses in Da, and OpenMS's coarse natural-abundance isotope envelope (isotope index, mass, share of molecules), or the reason there is none (an isotope-labeled structure, or an element OpenMS has no isotope data for)

np_likeness.description: Ertl et al. 2008 natural-product likeness, about -5 (synthetic-like) to 5 (natural-product-like), and the confidence: the share of the molecule's fragments the model knows

qed.description: QED (Bickerton 2012) with mean weights, maximum weights and unweighted; the eight inputs (MW average mass, ALOGP Crippen, HBA, HBD, PSA, ROTB, AROM, ALERTS) and each input's desirability; and the SMARTS of every unwanted group QED counted

rules.description: one entry per rule evaluated: id, label, passes, citation, and every clause with its property, bound and this molecule’s value. A rule with anyClauses passes when at least one of those holds

scaffold.description: the Bemis–Murcko scaffold (ring systems and linkers, side chains removed) as canonical SMILES, empty for a molecule with no ring; the generic framework (every atom carbon, every bond single), null where an atom has more bonds than carbon allows; and the indices of the atoms the scaffold keeps, on the implicit-hydrogen molecule

solubility.description: ESOL (Delaney 2004) log S in mol/L under two coefficient sets, rdkitRefit (Walters' refit to RDKit descriptors) and delaney2004 (the paper's, with Crippen logP for Daylight CLOGP), and the four inputs: Crippen logP, average mass, rotatable bonds, aromatic proportion

structure.description: the 2D structure every reading was taken on, drawn by RDKit with implicit hydrogens as the chemistry tab opens it

summary.description: the assessment in one sentence, generated from this run

synthetic_accessibility.description: Ertl & Schuffenhauer 2009 synthetic accessibility, 1 (easy) to 10 (hard), with its fragment score, complexity penalty, symmetry correction, the counts they read and how many fragments the table did not know; null only if the fragment table could not be loaded
